source.title: Invasive Ants Disrupt Gecko Pollination and Seed Dispersal of the Endangered Plant Roussea simplex in Mauritius

design: Within-island field experiment comparing naturally ant-infested flowers/fruits with ant-free controls and ant-removal/exclusion treatments in the critically endangered endemic Roussea simplex.

source_native_results.native_partner: Phelsuma cepediana is the documented sole pollinator and seed disperser in the focal system
source_native_results.interaction_effect: gecko visitation to ant-free and ant-removal/exclusion flowers and fruits was higher than to ant-infested flowers and fruits
source_native_results.reproductive_effect: seed set from ant-infested flowers was greatly reduced relative to ant-free control flowers
source_native_results.mechanistic_interpretation: aggressive Technomyrmex albipes interference prevents gecko access to flowers and fruits

observed_chain: invasive-ant interference -> reduced gecko access/visitation -> reduced seed set
claim_boundary: This is a within-island experimental perturbation rather than an archipelago transition. It validates qualitative propagation from interaction disruption to reproduction, not the ABM trait-position mechanism and not a universal invasive-ant effect.
